title: The boy in the tower
hook: his noble family locks him up to stop him becoming a Dominican

segments.voice: Yesterday, the final Amen: the Catechism closes where the Lord's Prayer closes, and that finished our long walk through the Catechism. Your line was amen. Where did you say it and mean it? Day one thousand one hundred fifty-two.

A young friar is on the road, walking in the white habit of a new preaching order. Then horsemen. His own brothers, soldiers, ride him down, the old lives say, and carry him home to the family castle. His family were nobles, and they had a plan for him: a respectable post in the Church, near home, with standing and land. Not this. Not a begging friar who owned nothing and preached wherever people would listen. So they shut him in, and waited for him to change his mind. His name was Thomas, and the world would come to call him Thomas Aquinas. Today we leave the Catechism behind and start a new block: Aquinas, explained plainly. It begins not with a book, but with a locked room.
screen: `A FRIAR ON THE ROAD.` → `HIS BROTHERS RIDE HIM DOWN.` → `SHUT IN AT HOME.`

segments.voice: Here is the story as the early lives of Thomas tell it. Tradition says the confinement lasted a long time, by some tellings a year or more. His mother wanted her son back. His brothers wanted the habit gone. Thomas stayed put, and stayed a Dominican. He didn't rage. He used the time. The old accounts say he read the Scriptures, studied Peter Lombard's book of theology called the Sentences, and taught his sisters. Tradition says one sister was so moved that she later gave her own life to God as a nun. Then the hard scene, told plainly. The brothers, the story goes, sent a woman into his room to pull him away from his vows. Thomas grabbed a burning stick from the fire and drove her out, then marked a cross on the wall with it. Tradition adds that he prayed, fell asleep, and dreamed of angels binding a cord around his waist, and that he was not troubled that way again. In the end the family gave up. One telling has him let down from a window in a basket, back to his brothers in the order. Why open a block about a great thinker here? Because the Summa, the long and careful book we're about to walk through, was written by a man who first had to decide what he was for. His family's plan wasn't wicked. It was sensible, even generous. His call was quieter and poorer. In Luke, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says: "No man putting his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God." Catholics honor Thomas as a saint and a Doctor of the Church. Before the arguments, there was a door he wouldn't let anyone close.
screen: `A YEAR OR MORE, TRADITION SAYS.` · `HE STUDIED AND TAUGHT HIS SISTERS.` · `A BURNING STICK, A CROSS ON THE WALL.` · `LET DOWN IN A BASKET, BACK TO HIS ORDER.` · then, large: `NO MAN PUTTING HIS HAND TO THE PLOUGH.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold to a calling. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one thing you've said yes to that matters: a vow, a vocation, a promise to a person, a piece of work you know is yours. Now notice what pulls against it today. Tiredness. Other people's plans for you. Your own second thoughts. Don't fight them. Just name them, one by one. Then come back to the yes, and rest your attention there. If you pray, you can ask God, in your own words, for the grace to keep it. If you don't, simply hold the yes, like a hand on a plough. The bell holds the time.
The boy in the tower. Thomas Aquinas, shut in at home by his own family, who came out still a Dominican. Today's word.
screen: `THE BOY IN THE TOWER — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: he kept his call. Today, when something pulls you away from your yes, do one small thing that keeps it. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-two.

howItsDone: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Thomas Aquinas each year, and Dominicans and Catholic schools often tell the story of his confinement when they speak about holding to a vocation.

options: give in and take the post they've planned.
stay, keep the habit, and use the time to study and teach.

fork.reveal: the old lives say he stayed put, studied, taught his sisters, and kept his vows, until the family gave up. no raging, no giving in.
